question: In uncomplicated Paget's disease of bone, serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) is markedly elevated while serum calcium remains normal (unless the patient is immobilised).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. This statement is TRUE. In active Paget's disease, ALP can be elevated 5–20 times the normal upper limit, reflecting the chaotic bone remodelling. Serum calcium is normal in ambulatory patients. Only prolonged immobilisation can tip the balance toward hypercalcaemia.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The key biochemical hallmark of Paget's disease is a markedly raised ALP (reflecting intense osteoblastic activity) with normal serum calcium. Hypercalcaemia only occurs in Paget's disease when the patient is immobilised (immobilisation hypercalcaemia) — an important complication to recognise.
